summary: Async scene loading with progress, and a minimum display time so the loading screen cannot flash.
overview: Call LoadScene and wire the progress event to a bar. It enforces a minimum display time, so a load that would finish in one frame does not flash the loading screen — a genuinely fast load still shows for at least that long.
useCases: Showing real progress rather than a fake bar.
Avoiding the jarring one-frame flash on fast loads.

params.tuning: Long enough to read, short enough not to annoy. Around a second is typical.

gotchas.title: Unity's progress stops at 0.9 until activation
gotchas.body: AsyncOperation.progress caps there when allowSceneActivation is false. A bar driven straight from it appears to stall just before finishing — which is why this one normalises it.
